parsedVerdict.reasoning: SchedulingService is a domain service. Its job is to enforce business rules (allowed visit length, blocked patients, practitioners who don't see minors, daily capacity, overlapping slots) and to manage the appointment lifecycle (cancel goes through the Appointment entity). It has no SQL, connection or transaction handling, HTTP or request handling, or framework code. The service does turn raw DAO records into entities itself (new Patient(...), new Practitioner(...), new Appointment(...), the 'as AppointmentStatus' cast and '{ ...candidate }' when saving). That leans toward persistence mapping, but it is thin glue around the DAO calls, not real persistence logic, so I don't count it as a misplaced responsibility. The direct imports and constructor injection of PatientDao and AppointmentDao are a dependency-direction issue, which is out of scope here.
